name: Institute of Contemporary Art San Francisco
note: Hand-modelled 2026-09-23 to the owner's own description of the structure: a black glass curtain-wall box, four red rectangular columns projecting diagonally out past its corners, and a flat red roof that overhangs the box but stops halfway along the columns, their tops flush with it. Was restyle 'chinatown' from 'rule 1: chinatown zone' (BUGS.md #118), which is what the owner saw as 'just a low brick building'.

name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts Gallery
note: Modelled from the OWNER'S OWN STRUCTURAL DESCRIPTION (2026-09-23) plus the front elevation he supplied, after two bails: the Metreon is across the street and in every photograph, every Mapillary frame shows the rear (BUGS.md #128), and this way is ONE polygon with no building:parts. An L-shaped, one-tall-level, windowless box of corrugated pale metal on a dark stone base, three glazed barrel vaults breaking the roofline at one end of the Mission Street front, the entrance at the far end, and a patio cut out of the far corner with the 'boat pitched down' glass structure and the rectangular fountain. Everything is derived from the ring: the L and the patio are the two biggest empty bounding-box corners, the front is the longer of the two arms flanking the re-entrant quadrant, and the three tangent vaults have radius = a sixth of the bay's front. No `front` bearing on purpose (BUGS.md #117): the builder uses no axis names. See src/render/landmarks/sf/ybca.ts; references in docs/shots/refs/sf-commons/24563073/. HEIGHT: OSM says 28 m; the owner's own description is ONE TALL LEVEL and the entrance photograph's canopy and doors scale a box of about sixteen metres, so 16 is used here, the same call as Rincon Annex above (BUGS.md #126, believed the photograph). At 28 the vault crowns cannot clear the parapet and the blank box reads as a warehouse. GROUND FLOOR IS LEVEL 2, the garden level (docs/YERBA-BUENA.md, the authoritative level model): the cladding, glazing and entrance start at the gardens builder's exported DECK_H and everything below it is the retaining face the entrance steps climb.

name: San Francisco Civic Center Courthouse
note: Rusticated podium, tall round-arched windows, plain upper storeys, balustraded roofline (Mapillary way-108389188-0{1,2,3}.jpg, all kept). The building's rounded corner pavilion carries a small dome the kit has no per-corner crown for; left off rather than invented as a whole-roof dome.

note: Rusticated stone block, giant composite pilasters at the corners, dentilled cornice, pedimented windows (Mapillary way-32859013-0{1,2,3}.jpg, all kept, corridor confirmed at the Washington/Battery corner in frame 03). name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
note: Hand-modelled 2026-09-23 (owner: 'SF MOMA absolutely needs to be hand-modeled, it is not a tenement building'). Botta's stepped brick mass with the sliced striped drum, Snohetta's rippled pale wing above and behind. Was restyle 'tenement' from 'rule 8: medium building (levels >= 4)'.

name: Metreon
note: Hand-modelled 2026-09-23 (owner: 'This is an important, but very strange area. We should do custom modeling.'). A blank pale metal-panel street elevation with a wall-sized METREON wordmark, a Target bullseye and an AMC/IMAX corner over a perforated dot panel, and an entirely different long glazed wall on the Yerba Buena Gardens side, which stands on the raised deck over Moscone Center (BUGS.md #130) — the garden glazing starts partway up the wall over a blank retaining wall to grade. Was `pending` in docs/sf-queue.csv, unclaimed.

name: Old Mission Dolores
note: Hand-modelled 2026-09-24: 1776 adobe, the oldest building in San Francisco. Very plain, very low, church() with front: 'mission' for the flat espadana parapet and bell niches. Not the neighbouring Mission Dolores Basilica (way/256442760), a separate, much larger building left untouched. No usable street photograph (Mapillary marked junk); form from the building's well-documented history.

name: Bimbo's 365 Club
note: Hand-modelled 2026-09-24: 1931 nightclub, 1025 Columbus Avenue. Low flat-roofed box, cream wall covered in a pierced circle-motif breeze-block screen (approximated as a dense punched grid), corner blade sign 'BIMBO'S' and a lit readerboard marquee at the entrance. No usable Mapillary frame (marked junk); confirmed by name via Wikimedia Commons (Bimbo's365Blade.jpg, Bimbo's Marquee.jpg, both at 1025 Columbus).
